title: Egypt Posts Record Q1 2026 Tourism Revenue of $5.1 Billion, Up 34%
detail: Egypt's tourism sector recorded its strongest-ever first quarter in 2026, welcoming 5.6 million visitors — a 43% year-on-year surge — and generating $5.1 billion in revenues, up 34% from $3.8 billion in Q1 2025. Officials attributed the surge partly to the Grand Egyptian Museum's full opening adjacent to the Giza pyramids and robust European and Gulf arrivals. A 16% year-on-year decline was noted in April arrivals as regional geopolitical instability linked to the Iran conflict dampened sentiment; Egypt is targeting 21 million annual arrivals for the full year.

title: Sisi Hosts OECD Secretary-General to Advance Egypt's Reform and Investment Agenda
detail: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi received OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann in Cairo, reaffirming Egypt's commitment to comprehensive economic reform aligned with OECD standards. The talks focused on deepening institutional cooperation, boosting foreign direct investment, and advancing Egypt's reform agenda under the IMF Extended Fund Facility. Egypt's February 2026 IMF review cited inflation falling to 11.9% in January 2026 and real GDP growth of 4.4% in FY2024/25 as key program achievements.
